title: Project Management MVP — SQLite schema
description: Source-of-truth schema document. SQLAlchemy models in app/models.py (Part 6) must mirror this 1:1. Edit this file FIRST, then the models, then the migration/seed.

conventions.ids: TEXT, 32-char uuid4 hex (no dashes). Generated by the application, never by SQLite.
conventions.timestamps: TEXT, ISO-8601 UTC with seconds precision and a trailing 'Z' (e.g. '2026-04-25T12:34:56Z'). Application-supplied; SQLite stores as TEXT.
conventions.booleans: Not used in this schema; if added later, store as INTEGER 0/1.
conventions.deletions: Hard delete with ON DELETE CASCADE through every FK. No soft-delete columns in MVP.
conventions.positions: INTEGER, contiguous 0..N-1 within a column or board. Re-packed in the same transaction as any move/insert/delete (see docs/db.md § Position handling).

tables.name: users
tables.purpose: One row per known username. The MVP seeds a single 'user' row whose id is referenced by the JWT 'sub' claim translation in app/auth.py.

columns.name: username
columns.comment: Matches the JWT sub claim. Lower-case, max 64 chars (validated in app, not DB).

columns.name: created_at
columns.comment: ISO-8601 UTC, set by app at insert.

indexes.name: ix_users_username
indexes.comment: Implicit from the UNIQUE constraint; listed for clarity.

tables.name: boards
tables.purpose: One board per user (MVP constraint). When the user is removed, the board and everything below it cascade away.

tables.name: columns
tables.purpose: Vertical lanes on a board. Title is editable. Order within a board is given by `position` (0..N-1).

indexes.name: ix_columns_board_position
indexes.comment: Read pattern: ORDER BY position WHERE board_id = ?. UNIQUE intentionally omitted for MVP (see db.md § Why position is not UNIQUE).

tables.name: cards
tables.purpose: Tasks placed in a column. `details` is plain text for MVP (no markdown rendering yet).

columns.name: details
columns.comment: Empty string allowed; NULL is not.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.comment: Bumped on every PATCH (title/details/column/position change). Useful for AI chat context (“most recently touched”).

indexes.name: ix_cards_column_position
indexes.comment: Read pattern: ORDER BY position WHERE column_id = ?.

tables.name: conversations
tables.purpose: One rolling conversation per user (MVP). Created lazily on first chat turn.

tables.name: messages
tables.purpose: Append-only chat log. The Part 9 chat endpoint persists both the user message and the assistant reply in the same transaction.

columns.name: content
columns.comment: Raw text. For assistant messages this is the `reply` field of the Structured Output, NOT the full JSON envelope.

indexes.name: ix_messages_conv_created
indexes.comment: Read pattern: most recent N messages for a conversation.

seed.trigger: Run on first app startup (and idempotently on every subsequent startup) by app.db.init_db().

cards.title: Align roadmap themes
cards.details: Draft quarterly themes with impact statements and metrics.

cards.title: Gather customer signals
cards.details: Review support tags, sales notes, and churn feedback.

cards.title: Prototype analytics view
cards.details: Sketch initial dashboard layout and key drill-downs.

cards.title: Refine status language
cards.details: Standardize column labels and tone across the board.

cards.title: Design card layout
cards.details: Add hierarchy and spacing for scanning dense lists.

cards.title: QA micro-interactions
cards.details: Verify hover, focus, and loading states.

cards.title: Ship marketing page
cards.details: Final copy approved and asset pack delivered.

cards.title: Close onboarding sprint
cards.details: Document release notes and share internally.

rows.conversations: Not seeded; created lazily on first chat turn.

seed.idempotency: init_db() checks for the existence of the seeded user by username. If it exists, no rows are inserted (no upserts, no deletes). This means a developer who edits a seeded card in the running app will keep their edit across restarts as long as the SQLite file persists; in the container the DB lives at /app/data/pm.db and is ephemeral.

wire_contract.notes: This shape matches frontend/src/lib/kanban.ts#BoardData byte-for-byte so the existing UI hook can swap from initialData to the API response with zero structural changes.
